questions.ask: Look at the date on C066, the Swiss 5 francs. Does it end in 6 or in 8?
questions.why: The phone photo reads 1976 but the record says 1978. Only the coin can settle it.

questions.ask: How many stars are on token T001 (the 20 play token with GR)?
questions.why: Its record says 13 stars; its twin T002 has 15. If they differ they are two different kinds.

questions.ask: Turn over C153, the 2008 UK 10 pence. Does the back show a crowned lion, or a piece of the Royal Shield?
questions.why: 2008 had both designs. The record lists the lion type.

questions.ask: East Caribbean coins are filed under the code EC, which is really Ecuador's code. Switch East Caribbean to XC?
questions.why: It only changes the short code in serial numbers (EC-... to XC-...), before the one-time serial renumbering.

questions.ask: Your Mercury dime album (A006): from your page photos it has 77 holes, but the record says about 80. Is 77 right?
questions.why: The 80 was an estimate. Only you can lower a count.

questions.ask: Do you have two UK 5 pence coins dated 1992?
questions.why: C169 (from the ledger) and C275 (added later from a photo) are both 1992 5p. They may be the same coin logged twice.

questions.ask: Please take a phone photo of C140's map side (Spain 2008 1 cent) and drop it in the STAGING folder.
questions.why: Spain's 1 cent changed design in 2010; the map side helps confirm the catalog number.

questions.ask: Look under the date on C053, the 2011 German 20 cent. Is the small letter an F or a J?
questions.why: The record says J (Hamburg); the phone photo looks more like F (Stuttgart).

questions.ask: On C206, the Japanese 1 yen, read the date characters at the bottom. Is it 四十六 (46) or 五十一 (51)?
questions.why: The record says 1976 (Showa 51); the photo looks like Showa 46 (1971).

questions.ask: Turn over C023, the 1918 iron 20 with the oak wreath. What words are on the other side?
questions.why: No German Empire 20 pfennig was struck in 1918, so it is probably a city's emergency money; the other side should name the city.

questions.ask: On C238, the 1973 D West German 2 mark, whose name is written next to the portrait: KONRAD ADENAUER or THEODOR HEUSS?
questions.why: They are two different coins (KM#124 Adenauer, KM#A127 Heuss) with different mintages; the record lists both.

questions.ask: On C088, the 1957 dime, look on the torch side, left of the torch near the bottom. Is there a small D?
questions.why: No letter means Philadelphia (160,160,000 struck); D means Denver (113,354,330). The record can't tell yet.

questions.ask: On C064, the Malta 2008 1 euro, is there a small F on the Maltese (cross) side?
questions.why: Catalogues list the 2008 Maltese 1 euro as struck in Paris with an F mint mark.

questions.ask: C073 is a tube of 26 1976 quarters. Keep it as one mixed lot, or sort it into no-letter and D piles?
questions.why: Philadelphia and Denver struck different numbers (809,784,016 and 860,118,839), so one mintage can't describe a mixed tube.

options.label: I'll sort it
options.free: How many with D, how many without?

questions.ask: A Britannia penny (George V) waits in STAGING: NOID_UnitedKingdom_1922_1Penny_rev.jpg. Is the date 1922 or 1932?
questions.why: The photo's name says 1922, but at full zoom the third digit looks like a 3 to Claude and to Gemini. The two years are different catalogue types, so the coin is not added until you say.

questions.ask: The 1990 5p photo in STAGING (NOID_UnitedKingdom_1990_Uncertain_obv.jpg): is it one of the two 1990 5p you already have (C167, C168), or a third one?
questions.why: C167 and C168 have no photo yet. Muse sent it as a new coin; if it is one of the two, adding it again would count it twice.

questions.ask: The 1988 penny photo in STAGING (NOID_UnitedKingdom_1988_1Penny_obv.jpg): is it C108, the 1988 penny you already have, or a second 1988 penny?
questions.why: C108 has no photo yet. Muse sent the photo as a new coin.

questions.ask: Italy 1979 50 lire: the new photo (NOID_Italy_1979_50Lire_obv.jpg, Oct 13) shows the Vulcan side, like C287's photo from Oct 8. Same coin, or a second 1979 50 lire?
questions.why: Muse sent it as a new coin; if it is C287 again it would be counted twice.

questions.ask: Italy 1978 50 lire: the new photo (NOID_Italy_1978_50Lire_obv.jpg, Oct 13) shows the Vulcan side, like C199's photo. Same coin, or a second 1978 50 lire?
questions.why: Muse sent it as a new coin; if it is C199 again it would be counted twice.
